name: Boys Town National Hotline
summary: 24/7 crisis support for youth and parents facing family problems, bullying, suicide, and more.

sections.title: About the Boys Town National Hotline
sections.text: The Boys Town National Hotline is a 24-hour crisis, resource, and referral line for children, teens, and parents facing various issues including family problems, bullying, abuse, suicide, and more. Run by Boys Town—a nonprofit organization founded in 1917 to help at-risk youth—the hotline provides free, confidential support from trained counselors who specialize in helping young people and families. The hotline has helped millions of callers since its founding and serves youth and families across the United States.

sections.title: Who the Hotline Serves
sections.text: The hotline serves both youth and parents. Young people can call about problems with parents, school stress, bullying, depression, abuse, running away, suicidal thoughts, substance use, relationships, and more. Parents can call for help with parenting challenges, communication issues, concerns about their child's behavior or mental health, and guidance on getting help for their family. There's no problem too big or too small—if you're struggling, the hotline is here to help.

sections.title: How to Reach the Hotline
sections.text: Call 1-800-448-3000 any time, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Text VOICE to 20121 to reach a crisis counselor via text. Spanish-speaking counselors are available. All calls are free and confidential. When you call, you'll speak with a trained Boys Town counselor who will listen to your concerns, help you work through the situation, and connect you with local resources if needed. There's no cost and no judgment.

sections.title: What Counselors Provide
sections.text: Boys Town counselors are trained in crisis intervention and can help with a wide range of issues affecting youth and families. Counselors provide emotional support, help callers work through problems and develop solutions, offer information about community resources, and can connect families with local services when needed. For youth in crisis, counselors can help create safety plans and provide ongoing support. Counselors use Boys Town's evidence-based model focused on building healthy relationships and communication skills.

sections.title: Boys Town Resources
sections.text: Beyond the hotline, Boys Town offers extensive resources for families including parenting tips and guides on the Boys Town website, a free parenting app, and information about Boys Town's residential and community programs for at-risk youth. Boys Town's parenting advice is based on decades of research and practice with children and families. The organization also offers direct care programs for youth who need more intensive support, including residential care, in-home family services, and school-based programs.
